title: Check yourself: creating custom exception classes

questions.stem: A plugin host calls each plugin's `onEvent(event)`, which its interface declares `throws Throwable`, inside `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { log.warn(...); }`, then moves on to the next plugin. One plugin author declares `class RateLimitHit extends Throwable`, so that nobody swallows it by accident, and throws it for one event. What does the host do?

options.text: It logs a warning and calls the next plugin, since onEvent declares Throwable and the host catches what onEvent declares
options.says: a catch clause handles only its own type and subtypes, whatever the method declares; RateLimitHit is not an Exception

options.text: It logs a warning and calls the next plugin, since extending Throwable makes RateLimitHit unchecked like a RuntimeException
options.says: a direct subclass of Throwable is checked, and it is not a RuntimeException, so catch (Exception e) doesn't see it

options.text: It logs nothing and leaves the loop, since RateLimitHit sits beside Exception in the hierarchy rather than under it
options.says: catch (Exception e) never sees a direct subclass of Throwable, so it leaves the loop and no later plugin runs

options.text: It logs nothing and leaves the loop, since a throwable outside Exception's hierarchy makes the JVM stop the host's thread
options.says: the JVM stops nothing by itself; the throwable leaves the loop because the catch clause names Exception, and a caller further up can still catch it

origin.section: The Class You Extend Decides Who Must Handle It

questions.stem: An import job catches `IOException e`, whose message is `disk full`, and throws `new ImportFailedException(e)`, using the constructor that takes only a `Throwable` and passes it to `super`. What is the first line of the stack trace the job logs?

options.text: `ImportFailedException: java.io.IOException: disk full`, since the message is set to the cause's toString()
options.says: the (cause) constructor takes cause.toString() as its detail message

options.text: `ImportFailedException: disk full`, since the message is set to the cause's getMessage()
options.says: the message is cause.toString(), which includes the cause's class name

options.text: `ImportFailedException`, since the message stays null when only a cause is passed
options.says: only the () constructor, or a null cause, leaves the message null

options.text: `ImportFailedException: null`, since the message stays null and prints as the word null
options.says: the message is cause.toString(), not null; and when a message is null, toString() prints only the class name

origin.section: A Wrapper Keeps the Original Failure Only If It Is Given the Cause

questions.stem: `PricingFailedException` keeps `private final transient PriceList priceList;` (`PriceList` is not `Serializable`) and its `getSku()` returns `priceList.sku()`. The batch framework sends failures to the scheduler with Java serialization, and the scheduler calls `getSku()` to plan a retry. What happens?

options.text: The exception arrives and getSku() throws NullPointerException, since a transient field is left out of the bytes and reads as null
options.says: a transient field is skipped when writing, so it reads as null on the other side

options.text: The exception arrives and getSku() returns the SKU, since a transient field is set again by the constructor when it is read
options.says: deserializing a Serializable class does not run its constructor; the transient field stays null

options.text: Sending fails with NotSerializableException, since a transient field's type is still checked before anything is written
options.says: transient fields are skipped, so their type is never checked; that is why transient silences the error

options.text: Sending fails with NotSerializableException, since a transient field still refers to a type that can't be written
options.says: a transient field is skipped when writing, so what it refers to is never written

origin.section: Every Exception Is Serializable, So Its Fields Must Be Too

questions.stem: A developer writes `class Pipeline<T> { class StageFailedException extends RuntimeException { StageFailedException(String m) { super(m); } } }` so that each stage's failure is declared next to the pipeline. What does javac say?

options.text: It reports an error, since a class nested in Pipeline<T> without static counts as generic
options.says: an inner class of a generic class is implicitly generic, and a generic class may not extend Throwable

options.text: It reports an error, since a class nested in Pipeline<T> can't call super(m) from its constructor
options.says: a nested exception class calls super like any other; a static nested exception class inside Pipeline<T> compiles

options.text: It compiles cleanly, since StageFailedException declares no type parameter, whatever Pipeline<T> declares
options.says: the inner class picks up T from Pipeline<T>, so it counts as generic

options.text: It compiles with an unchecked warning, since Pipeline<T>'s T only makes a catch of the nested class unchecked
options.says: a generic Throwable subclass is a compile error, not a warning

origin.section: An Exception Class Can't Be Generic

questions.stem: `ProductNotFoundException` calls `super(message, null, false, false)`, because catalogue lookups miss thousands of times a second. Months later the repository also throws it when a database row points at a deleted product, and it reaches the error log through `log.error("lookup failed", e)`. What does the log show for it?

options.text: Only the class name and the message, since the trace is empty from construction on
options.says: with writableStackTrace = false no trace is captured, so printing it shows no at lines

options.text: Only the class name, the message and the throw site, since the throw site is recorded later, at the throw
options.says: the trace is captured at construction or not at all; throwing records nothing, so no frame is printed

options.text: The full trace, since printing walks the stack when the trace is empty
options.says: the trace is captured at construction or never; printing doesn't walk the stack

options.text: The full trace, since those arguments only block changes made later
options.says: writableStackTrace = false also stops the capture at construction, so the trace starts empty

origin.section: Filling In the Stack Trace Is Most of the Cost; Skip It Only Where Nobody Reads the Trace
